topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the main themes of inflammatory initiation, cellular mechanisms, and resolution.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition by PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental principles by which the innate immune system detects infections and tissue damage through conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors across cellular compartments.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus specifically on the biology of Toll-like receptors, detailing their ligand specificity, structural properties, and spatially regulated intracellular signaling cascades.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover cytosolic danger-sensing receptor families and the multi-protein inflammasome complex that processes pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Cellular orchestration and systemic impacts of the inflammatory response
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sentinel cells initiate the acute inflammatory response by driving leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic drainage, and potentially dangerous systemic physiological reactions.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how acute inflammation is terminated, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how persistent threats lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
